triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The 6.2 percent OASDI tax was computed on a TaxUnit entity even though 26 USC 3101(a) imposes it 'on the income of every individual' on that individual's own wages, so a multi-earner tax unit would have had its members' wages pooled into one tax base instead of taxed person by person.
triage.triage_notes: Provision read through the pinned corpus (us/statute/26/3101): '(a) ... there is hereby imposed on the income of every individual a tax equal to 6.2 percent of the wages (as defined in section 3121(a)) received by the individual with respect to employment'. Decisive change is entity: TaxUnit -> Person on oasdi_wage_tax. The same diff also rewrote the module summary, switched proof-atom keys span->excerpt, retyped the rate atom parameter->amount, added a self-import atom for the rate, and reordered the formula to 'oasdi_wage_tax_rate * wages' (commutative, no meaning change); those parts are provenance/mechanical. Commit message body is empty and the subject is generic ('Refresh payroll generated rules'); PR #328 has no reviews or review comments, so no maintainer text names the entity defect - confidence capped below 0.8. Companion test a.test.yaml was also rewritten (rate assertions dropped from that file) even though the PR body claims oracle-parameter assertions were added for the 3101(a) rate; not a module defect but worth noting.
triage.verifier_justification: The only line in the diff that changes encoded meaning is `entity: TaxUnit` -> `entity: Person` on the `oasdi_wage_tax` derived rule; everything else is provenance or cosmetic (summary rewritten, proof-atom `span`->`excerpt` and `kind: parameter`->`amount`, two added proof atoms, `'0.062'` reflowed to a block scalar, and `wages * oasdi_wage_tax_rate` -> `oasdi_wage_tax_rate * wages`, which is commutative). The pinned corpus text for us/statute/26/3101 reads "there is hereby imposed on the income of every individual a tax equal to 6.2 percent of the wages ... received by the individual with respect to employment", so the pre-fix module declared a broader computation/output entity than the excerpt it itself cited — a scope disagreement with the source, not new coverage or a policy choice. Corroborating that this is the encoder's own scope-fidelity class: `validator_pipeline.py` carries entity-scope checks keyed to who the source imposes the amount on (e.g. `find_employer_scoped_entity_issues`: "is declared on `{entity}`, but the source text imposes the amount, tax, credit, or limitation on an employer"), and the same commit made the parallel 3111 Business->Employer corrections. I tried the mechanical, not_a_defect, and alternative-kind readings and none survive: no formula, parameter, version, or effective date moved, and the one surviving semantic edit is squarely entity scope.
triage.verifier_notes: Reviewer notes. (1) The first reader's supporting quote is weak evidence: "refresh generated RuleSpec artifacts for the Chapter 21 FICA wage/tax chain..." is generic PR boilerplate (PR #328) and says nothing about entities; the PR body never mentions entity corrections at all. The decisive evidence is the diff line itself, so the case survives but the stored quote should be swapped for the `entity:` hunk. (2) The first reader's rationale ("a multi-earner tax unit would have had its members' wages pooled into one tax base instead of taxed person by person") overstates the numeric harm for THIS module: the rule is a flat 6.2% with no cap, so 6.2% of pooled wages equals the sum of per-person taxes. The real defect is the declared entity/output surface (per-person attribution, and correctness once the 3121(a)(1) wage base enters the chain), not an arithmetic error. Kind and verdict are unaffected. (3) The companion test statutes/26/3101/a.test.yaml was rewritten but uses single scalar wage inputs, so it does not independently discriminate Person vs TaxUnit; it is not corroboration. (4) The rule_names list includes `oasdi_wage_tax_rate`, whose changes are purely mechanical (proof-atom kind/excerpt rename plus block-scalar reflow of the same 0.062). Only `oasdi_wage_tax` carries the defect; rule_path rules[oasdi_wage_tax].entity is correct. (5) Non-blocking caveat checked and rejected: validator_pipeline has a documented carve-out allowing a TaxUnit-level Money rule whose statute says "individual" (`_taxunit_money_rule_can_use_individual_tax_credit_amount_source`), but it is scoped to final tax-credit amounts against tax, not an employee tax imposed on each individual's own wages. (6) Source read through the pinned release us-rulespec-2026-07-13, provision sha256 3fa3fc0b75faa2701c24747d44bf2a351beec597d7ef67823f6b4e78452300a0.
